10.1016/j.jacc.2026.10.058.title: High Bleeding Risk and Aspirin Omission at the Time of Primary PCI in STEMI: A Post Hoc Analysis of the PREMIUM Trial
10.1016/j.jacc.2026.10.058.abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with ST-segment–elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) at high bleeding risk (HBR) are also at increased risk of ischemic events, making the optimal antiplatelet therapy challenging. Whether HBR identifies patients who may benefit from upfront aspirin omission at the time of primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains unclear. OBJECTIVES: To evaluate whether HBR modifies the effect of aspirin omission in STEMI patients undergoing primary PCI. METHODS: The PREMIUM trial randomized patients with STEMI before primary PCI to low-dose prasugrel monotherapy or dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) with aspirin plus prasugrel. In the DAPT group, patients meeting Academic Research Consortium–HBR (ARC-HBR) criteria were permitted to discontinue aspirin at 3 months, whereas non-HBR patients were intended to continue DAPT for 12 months. This post hoc analysis assessed the primary outcome of a 12-month composite of all-cause death, stroke, or myocardial infarction and the major secondary outcome of Bleeding Academic Research Consortium (BARC) type 3 or 5 bleeding according to HBR status. RESULTS: Among 2,189 patients, 786 (35.9%) met ARC-HBR criteria. HBR patients had higher rates of the primary outcome (16.2% vs 6.2%; hazard ratio [HR], 2.68; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.05–3.52) and the major secondary outcome (10.9% vs 4.9%; HR, 2.28; 95% CI, 1.65–3.14). The primary outcome occurred with monotherapy versus DAPT in 18.0% versus 14.5% of HBR patients (HR, 1.29; 95% CI, 0.91–1.82) and 7.4% versus 5.0% of non-HBR patients (HR, 1.55; 95% CI, 1.01–2.37; P for interaction = 0.51). The major secondary outcome occurred in 9.2% versus 12.5% of HBR patients (HR, 0.71; 95% CI, 0.46–1.11) and 3.8% versus 6.1% of non-HBR patients (HR, 0.62; 95% CI, 0.38–1.00; P for interaction = 0.67). CONCLUSIONS: ARC-HBR identified patients with a substantially higher overall risk after primary PCI for STEMI but did not identify a subgroup with a more favorable treatment effect of upfront aspirin omission. Clinically meaningful treatment-effect modification cannot be excluded because of limited precision. These findings do not support using HBR status alone to guide upfront aspirin omission and should be interpreted in the context of the low-dose prasugrel regimen used in Japan. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT05709626

10.1016/j.jcin.2026.10.001.title: Rotational Atherectomy Plus Intravascular Lithotripsy Versus Intravascular Lithotripsy Alone for Coronary Calcified Nodules: The NODULE-SHOCK Trial
10.1016/j.jcin.2026.10.001.abstract: BACKGROUND: Optimal lesion preparation for coronary calcified nodules (CNs) and intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) pulse delivery for severe calcification remain uncertain. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate phenotype-specific calcium modification in severe calcification with and without CNs. METHODS: In this single-center randomized trial using a new-generation coronary IVL catheter, patients with optical coherence tomography-defined CNs (Cohort A) were assigned 1:1 to rotational atherectomy (RA) plus IVL or IVL alone; patients with severe calcification without CNs (Cohort B) were assigned 1:1 to maximum or operator-determined IVL pulses. Primary endpoints were minimum stent area (MSA) at the CN site in Cohort A and at the maximum calcium arc site in Cohort B. RESULTS: Among 120 patients, 66 (55%) were in Cohort A (33 per group) and 54 (45%) in Cohort B (27 per group). MSA at the CN site was 7.41 ± 2.12 mm2 with RA plus IVL vs 6.23 ± 1.55 mm2 with IVL alone (mean difference: 1.18 mm2; 95% CI: 0.27-2.09; P = 0.012). In Cohort B, MSA at the maximum calcium arc site was 5.50 ± 1.19 mm2 with maximum IVL pulses vs 5.56 ± 1.45 mm2 with operator-determined IVL pulses (mean difference: −0.06 mm2; 95% CI: −0.78 to 0.67; P = 0.873). CONCLUSIONS: RA plus IVL increased final stent area vs IVL alone in CN lesions, whereas maximum IVL pulses did not significantly increase final stent area compared with operator-determined pulses in severe calcification without CNs. These findings warrant validation in larger multicenter trials with clinical endpoints. (Coronary Calcified Nodule Management With Rotational Atherectomy Plus Shockwave Intravascular Lithotripsy vs Intravascular Lithotripsy Alone: A Prospective, Randomized Trial [NODULE-SHOCK]; ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT07000045)

10.1016/j.jcin.2026.09.030.title: Sirolimus- Versus Everolimus-Eluting Stents With Contemporary PCI in Three-Vessel Disease: The Multivessel TALENT Randomized Noninferiority Trial
10.1016/j.jcin.2026.09.030.abstract: BACKGROUND: Contemporary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) has improved outcomes in three-vessel disease (3VD). However, the Supraflex Cruz sirolimus-eluting stent (SES) has not been compared with the SYNERGY everolimus-eluting stent (EES) in this setting. OBJECTIVES: We compared the performance of the Supraflex Cruz SES and the SYNERGY EES in patients with de novo 3VD undergoing contemporary PCI. METHODS: We randomized 1,548 patients to the Supraflex Cruz SES (n=774) or the SYNERGY EES (n=774). Patients were selected after Heart Team discussion incorporating the SYNTAX Score II. Contemporary PCI included angiography-derived physiology, intravascular imaging optimization, CTO expertise, and short DAPT followed by prasugrel monotherapy. The primary endpoint was the 1-year patient-oriented composite endpoint (POCE: all-cause death, any stroke, any myocardial infarction, or any revascularization), estimated by Kaplan–Meier in the intention-to-treat population. The non-inferiority margin was 4.28%. RESULTS: Median follow-up was 367 days (IQR, 362–372). At 1 year, POCE was 15.23% (95% CI, 12.87–17.96) with Supraflex Cruz SES and 14.51% (95% CI, 12.20–17.21) with SYNERGY EES. The risk difference was 0.72 percentage points; the one-sided 95% upper confidence bound was 3.71%, below the margin (P non-inferiority=0.025). Myocardial infarction occurred in 10.07% (95% CI, 8.14–12.43) versus 8.14% (95% CI, 6.41–10.33), revascularization in 6.40% (95% CI, 4.86–8.40) versus 6.81% (95% CI, 5.22–8.87), and stent thrombosis in 1.31% (95% CI, 0.71–2.43) versus 1.08% (95% CI, 0.54–2.14). CONCLUSIONS: In patients with 3VD undergoing contemporary PCI, the Supraflex Cruz SES was noninferior to the SYNERGY EES for 1-year POCE. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT04390672

10.1016/j.jcin.2026.10.024.title: Thirty-Day Outcomes of a Dedicated Transcatheter Occlusion Device for Paravalvular Leak Closure: The PARADIGM Study
10.1016/j.jcin.2026.10.024.abstract: BACKGROUND: Paravalvular leak (PVL) is a complication of surgical valve replacement and is associated with poor prognosis. Percutaneous device closure offers a less invasive alternative to repeat surgery. OBJECTIVE: Evaluate the Amplatzer Valvular Plug III (APVL3) for PVL closure after surgical implant of a mechanical or bioprosthetic valve. METHODS: PARADIGM is a prospective, multicenter, single-arm study assessing transcatheter PVL closure. The primary endpoint was a composite of safety and effectiveness measures evaluating the implant success, PVL reduction ≥2 grades on exit from the procedure, procedural mortality, and device-related reinterventions through 30 days. Descriptive safety and performance endpoints were evaluated at 30 days. RESULTS: A total of 200 patients were enrolled across 24 sites in the United States, Europe, and Canada. Average age was 67.7+/-11.5 years, 58.5% were male, and 70.0% had a mechanical valve. Median(IQR) logistic EuroSCORE was 5.2(3.2,10.3), median(IQR) STS PROM was 2.9%(1.4,5.4), and 53.1%(104/196) were NYHA class III/IV. Heart failure was the primary indication for PVL closure (89.5%), and 65.0% were treated for mitral PVL. Successful implantation was achieved in 96.0%(192/200), with no procedural mortality. The primary endpoint was met in 94.0%(188/200), exceeding the performance goal(P<0.0001). The 30-day procedural success was 77.3%(140/181). At 30 days, mortality was 2.0%(4/200,95%CI:0.5-5.0), hemolytic anemia occurred in 3.5%(7/200,95% CI:1.42%,7.08%), 95.7%(156/163) had mild or less PVL, 82.7%(143/173) were NYHA class I/II, and KCCQ-OS improved by 15.7(12.6,18.8) points. CONCLUSION: PARADIGM met its primary endpoint, with favorable short-term outcomes. The results support this transcatheter device as a promising therapeutic option for PVL closure. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT04489823

10.1016/j.jcin.2026.10.023.title: 1-Year Safety and Effectiveness of a Next-Generation Dual-Seal Left Atrial Appendage Occluder
10.1016/j.jcin.2026.10.023.abstract: BACKGROUND: Left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) is a stroke prevention alternative for patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) intolerant to long-term oral anticoagulation (OAC). The next-generation dual-seal device was designed to improve operator ease of use while maintaining effective LAAO of the predicate device. OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this analysis was to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of a next-generation device through 1 year. METHODS: VERITAS is a single-arm, prospective, global, multicenter study. Patients with nonvalvular AF with an increased thromboembolism risk seeking a nonpharmacologic alternative to OAC were enrolled. One-year descriptive endpoints are provided, including mortality, neurological events, major bleeding, and device-related complications. One-year cardiac imaging was assessed for peridevice leak and device-related thrombus (DRT). RESULTS: Complete left atrial appendage (LAA) closure (0 mm leak) was observed in 91.1% (95% CI: 87.9%-93.7%) of patients by either transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) or cardiac computed tomography and 96.3% (95% CI: 93.2%-98.2%) by TEE alone. The cumulative DRT rate was 3.3% (95% CI: 2.0%-5.3%) with only 0.4% (95% CI: 0.1%-1.5%) deemed clinically relevant. One-year key clinical outcome rates are as follows: all-cause mortality: 3.9% (95% CI: 2.4%-6.3%); cardiovascular mortality: 1.9% (95% CI: 0.9%-3.8%); major bleeding: 6.6% (95% CI: 4.5%-9.2%); ischemic stroke or systemic embolism: 1.8% (95% CI: 0.8%-3.3%); pericardial effusion requiring intervention: 0.9% (95% CI: 0.3%-2.1%). No (0%) device embolization occurred. Median follow-up was 365 days (IQR: 349-380 days). CONCLUSIONS: The VERITAS study results support the 1-year safety and effectiveness of the next-generation device. (Abbott Medical-VERITAS Study; NCT06707688)

10.1016/j.jcin.2026.10.025.title: Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve-in-Valve and Valve-in-Ring Implantation: the TRIVIR registry
10.1016/j.jcin.2026.10.025.abstract: BACKGROUND: Transcatheter tricuspid valve-in-valve (TViV) and valve-in-ring (TViR) procedures are increasingly used; however, data on clinical outcomes, valve performance, and symptomatic improvement remain limited. OBJECTIVES: To evaluate a real-world multicenter cohort undergoing transcatheter TViV and TViR procedures. METHODS: We conducted an international multicenter registry including patients undergoing TViV/TViR procedures. The TRIVIR Registry evaluated all-cause mortality and a composite endpoint (CE), defined as all-cause mortality, heart failure (HF) hospitalization, and tricuspid bioprosthesis degeneration during follow-up. RESULTS: Between 2012 and 2025, 75 patients underwent TViV (n=62) or TViR (n=13) across 16 centers using Sapien (88%) or Myval (12%) valves. Median follow up was 1.86 years (IQR 0.10-2.59). Mean age was 62±13 years, and 69% were women. NYHA class III–IV decreased from 72% at baseline to 13% at 1-3 months and remained low during follow-up. No 30-day deaths occurred, while periprocedural complications occurred in 24% of procedures, mostly minor (17.3%). At 3 years, the Kaplan–Meier estimates of all-cause mortality and CE were 35.6% and 42.9%, and the cumulative incidences of HF hospitalization and tricuspid bioprosthesis degeneration were 16.6% and 11.4%, respectively. Patients who died had markers of advanced disease, including higher NT-proBNP levels, greater diuretic requirements, more frequent pacing/CRT implantation, and higher procedural complication rates. CONCLUSIONS: TViV/TViR represents a viable treatment strategy and provided sustained symptomatic improvement in high-risk patients. Patients who died exhibited a more advanced clinical profile, highlighting the importance of appropriate patient selection, early referral, and treatment in experienced centers.

10.1016/j.jcin.2026.10.002.title: TECTONIC CAD: Pivotal IDE Evaluation of Coronary Intravascular Lithotripsy for Severely Calcified Lesions
10.1016/j.jcin.2026.10.002.abstract: BACKGROUND: Severe coronary calcification complicates percutaneous coronary intervention by limiting lesion compliance and impairing stent expansion. OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the safety and effectiveness of the SonicForce Coronary Intravascular Lithotripsy System (Abbott Vascular) in severely calcified de novo coronary lesions. METHODS: TECTONIC CAD intravascular lithotripsy investigational device exemption (NCT06885177) was a prospective, multicenter, single-arm study of 335 patients at 40 U.S. centers. The primary safety endpoint was 30-day target lesion failure, defined as cardiac death, target-vessel myocardial infarction, or clinically driven target lesion revascularization. The primary effectiveness endpoint was procedural success. Each endpoint was tested against a prespecified performance goal. A prespecified optical coherence tomography (OCT) substudy evaluated calcium modification and stent expansion. RESULTS: A total of 335 patients were included in the full analysis set, with 330 and 334 as the evaluable populations for the primary safety and primary effectiveness endpoints, respectively, and a median follow-up duration of 36 days (Q1-Q3: 28-37 days). Thirty-day target lesion failure was 0.3% (1 of 330; exact 2-sided 95% CI: 0.0%-1.7%); the upper 1-sided 97.5% confidence bound was 1.7%, below the 12.9% performance goal (P < 0.0001). Procedural success was 97.0% (324 of 334; exact 2-sided 95% CI: 94.6%-98.6%); the lower 1-sided 97.5% confidence bound was 94.6%, above the 87.1% performance goal (P < 0.0001). In the OCT substudy, mean calcium length was 22.2 ± 10.3 mm, and the maximum contiguous calcium site had a calcium arc of 247.3 ± 99.0° and a thickness of 0.90 ± 0.25 mm at baseline. At this site, final stent area was 7.1 ± 1.9 mm2, with stent expansion of 95.9% ± 18.6%. Calcium fracture was identified in 62.5% (50 of 80) of lesions after intravascular lithotripsy and 66.3% (53 of 80) after stenting. CONCLUSIONS: TECTONIC CAD met both prespecified coprimary safety and effectiveness endpoints, demonstrating low 30-day target lesion failure and high procedural success. OCT demonstrated calcium fracture and favorable stent expansion at maximum contiguous calcium.

10.1016/j.atherosclerosis.2026.121940.title: Prognostic Value of 13N-Ammonia PET–Derived Myocardial Flow Reserve and Its Association With Peripheral Arterial Flow Impairment and Aortic Stiffness in Hemodialysis Patients
10.1016/j.atherosclerosis.2026.121940.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Hemodialysis patients carry markedly elevated cardiovascular mortality risk, yet validated prognostic tools remain limited. We investigated whether 13N-ammonia PET-derived myocardial flow reserve (MFR) independently predicts all-cause mortality and whether upstroke time (UT) and brachial-ankle pulse wave velocity (baPWV) are independent determinants of Global MFR. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 207 hemodialysis patients (median age 73 years, 65% male) who underwent 13N-ammonia PET between May 2013 and May 2024 (median follow-up 1,487 days). Prognostic value was assessed by multivariable Cox regression and incremental value indices. Determinants of Global MFR were evaluated by multivariable linear regression simultaneously adjusting for UT and baPWV. RESULTS: During follow-up, 100 patients (48%) died. Global MFR independently predicted all-cause mortality (hazard ratio 0.26, 95% CI 0.15–0.45, p < 0.001; C-statistic 0.724) with significant incremental value beyond clinical risk factors (ΔAUC +0.060, NRI +0.303, IDI +0.060; all p < 0.05). In multivariable linear regression (N = 196), both UT (β = −0.040 per 10 ms, p < 0.001) and baPWV (β = −0.015 per 100 cm/s, p = 0.006) were independent determinants of Global MFR (R2 = 0.236), despite being only weakly correlated (ρ = 0.069). Exploratory analyses showed stronger MFR associations with cardiovascular death (HR 0.195, p = 0.0008) than all-cause mortality. CONCLUSIONS: In hemodialysis patients, 13N-ammonia PET–derived Global MFR independently predicts all-cause mortality with incremental prognostic value beyond established risk factors. Both UT and baPWV are independently associated with lower Global MFR, suggesting that peripheral arterial flow impairment and aortic stiffness may each contribute to impaired coronary flow reserve.

10.1016/j.atherosclerosis.2026.121939.title: Role of Neutrophil Extracellular Traps in Atherosclerosis
10.1016/j.atherosclerosis.2026.121939.abstract: Neutrophils perform an important antimicrobial function through processes such as neutrophil extracellular trap formation (NETosis). In addition to infections, NETosis has also been observed in sterile inflammatory processes such as atherosclerosis, in which factors within the plaque such as oxidized lipids, complement, inflammatory cytokines, and immune complexes can induce NETosis. NETosis contributes importantly to atherosclerotic plaque formation through multiple mechanisms. These include endothelial cell activation leading to increased leukocyte transmigration into the subintimal space. NETs also promote activation of immune cells such as monocytes, macrophages, and T cells within the developing plaque, and contribute to the developing necrotic core through inducing apoptosis of monocytes/macrophages. Within advanced atherosclerotic plaques, evidence suggests that NETosis promotes thinning and rupture of the protective fibrous cap through induction of smooth muscle cell apoptosis and degradation of the extracellular matrix. Atherosclerotic plaque rupture leads to clot formation and clinical sequelae of atherosclerosis, with extracellular histones and myeloperoxidase released in NETosis contributing to this pro-thrombotic milieu. Taken together, NETosis appears to play an important role in multiple key aspects of atherogenesis and advanced plaque instability, thus representing a viable therapeutic target for ongoing clinical trials.

10.1016/j.atherosclerosis.2026.121945.title: High Cardiorespiratory Fitness predicts lower Risk of Progression and higher Chance of Regression of Arteriopathy during a Lifestyle Intervention
10.1016/j.atherosclerosis.2026.121945.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: High carotid intima–media thickness (cIMT) is a marker of arterial injury, and cIMT can be used to track the regression, arrest, or progression of arteriopathy. Because high cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF) protects from cardiovascular disease and closely associates with mitochondrial function, we determined whether baseline CRF and change in CRF predict change in cIMT during a lifestyle intervention. METHODS: A total of 208 subjects at risk for type 2 diabetes who participated in the Tübingen Lifestyle Intervention Program underwent measurements of CRF, cIMT, glucose, and lipid metabolism, body fat mass and distribution, and liver fat content at baseline and after 9 months. RESULTS: During the intervention, almost all cardiometabolic risk parameters improved. However, there was a large variability in the change in cIMT. In a multivariable linear regression model, CRF at baseline (std.-ß –0.19, p=0.02) and change in CRF (std.-ß −0.18, p=0.01) were associated with change in cIMT. Subjects in the upper tertile of change in cIMT had a mean (SD) increase in cIMT of 14 (9)%, while subjects in the lower tertile had a mean decrease in cIMT of 16 (7)%. Larger increase in CRF was associated with lower odds of progression of cIMT (OR per SD increase 0.05 [95% CI 0.006−0.42], p=0.004) and with higher chance of regression of cIMT (OR per SD increase 13 [95% CI 2−111], p=0.01). CONCLUSIONS: We provide novel findings that measuring CRF before and during a lifestyle intervention may help predict the progression and regression of arteriopathy.

10.1016/j.atherosclerosis.2026.121946.title: Angio-IMR Alone Is Not Enough: A Survival Tree for Risk Stratification in CCS
10.1016/j.atherosclerosis.2026.121946.abstract: BACKGROUND: The prognostic value of the angiography-derived index of microcirculatory resistance (Angio-IMR) in chronic coronary syndrome (CCS) remains unclear, particularly regarding its interaction with other clinical variables. METHODS: We enrolled 1415 CCS patients who underwent coronary angiography and were followed for 2 years for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). A survival tree was applied within the Angio-IMR-high subgroup to identify prognostic factors, and four risk groups were derived. Multivariable Cox regression and bootstrap resampling were used for model validation. The net reclassification improvement (NRI) was calculated to assess the incremental prognostic value beyond Angio-IMR alone. RESULTS: The survival tree identified NT-proBNP, age, and coronary stenosis severity as splitting variables, forming a stepwise risk gradient: the very-low-risk group (n=223, 0% MACE), the low-risk group (n=704, 4.0%), the intermediate-risk group (n=389, reference, 7.5%), and the high-risk group (n=99, 19.2%). After multivariable adjustment, the high-risk group remained independently associated with a significantly higher risk of MACE (HR 2.41, 95%CI 1.30–4.46, P=0.005), whereas the low-risk group had a lower risk (HR 0.54, 95%CI 0.32–0.91, P=0.020). The tree-derived groups significantly improved risk reclassification compared with Angio-IMR alone (NRI 0.309, 95%CI 0.183–0.549, P=0.001). Notably, systemic inflammatory markers (SIRI, NLR) increased stepwise across the groups (both P <0.001), paralleling the risk gradient. An online risk calculator was developed based on these findings (https://heartlab.shinyapps.io/calculator/). CONCLUSION: Angio-IMR alone does not adequately stratify risk in CCS. Integrating it with NT-proBNP, age, and coronary stenosis severity via a survival tree significantly improves 2-year MACE prediction, enabling precision targeting of preventive therapies.

10.1016/j.atherosclerosis.2026.121941.title: Non-HDL cholesterol as a lipid control target in severe hypercholesterolemia in primary care: a sex-stratified analysis
10.1016/j.atherosclerosis.2026.121941.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Non-HDL cholesterol (non-HDL-C) is recognized as a co-primary lipid target by the 2019 ESC/EAS guidelines, yet its attainment in patients with severe hypercholesterolemia (SH) in primary care remains poorly characterized. We aimed to assess non-HDL-C goal attainment in SH, examine LDL-C/non-HDL-C discordance, and evaluate sex differences in treatment and lipid control. METHODS: Cross-sectional, multicenter study using electronic health records from 156,082 adults attending 69 primary care centers in Madrid (2018–2021). SH was defined as total cholesterol ≥300 mg/dL or LDL-C ≥220 mg/dL. Non-HDL-C goal was <100 mg/dL per ESC/EAS 2019. Discordance was defined as LDL-C <70 mg/dL with non-HDL-C ≥100 mg/dL. Sex-stratified multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors of goal attainment. RESULTS: Of 6,071 patients with SH, only 228 (3.8%) achieved non-HDL-C <100 mg/dL. Men received high/very high intensity lipid-lowering therapy (LLT) more often than women (34.1% vs 26.0%; p<0.001), yet non-HDL-C levels were higher in men across all treatment categories except very high intensity. Among patients with established ASCVD, men achieved the target more often than women at both the <100 mg/dL (13.9% vs 6.1%; p=0.001) and <85 mg/dL thresholds (7.8% vs 2.6%; p=0.022). LDL-C/non-HDL-C discordance was identified in 21.3% of patients with LDL-C <70 mg/dL, more frequently in men (31.8% vs 13.8%; p=0.006), and increased with triglyceride levels. LLT intensity was not independently associated with goal attainment; diabetes, age, obesity, and ASCVD were the main predictors. CONCLUSIONS: Non-HDL-C goal attainment is critically low in SH patients in primary care, independently of treatment intensity. Sex disparities were significant, particularly in secondary prevention. Systematic non-HDL-C monitoring via electronic records and greater use of combination LLT are needed.

10.1016/j.atherosclerosis.2026.121944.title: Atherosclerotic events and acute pancreatitis incidence across the full range of plasma triglycerides in four large cohorts
10.1016/j.atherosclerosis.2026.121944.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: We tested the hypothesis that triglycerides at most levels are associated with higher incidence of ASCVD than acute pancreatitis. METHODS: We examined individuals from the Copenhagen City Heart Study (CCHS) 1976-78 (n=14,292; a median follow-up of 24 years) and 1991-94 (n=10,093; 20 years), the Copenhagen General Population Study (CGPS) 2003-15 (n=107,297; 13 years), the UK Biobank 2006-10 (n= 468,964; 14 years), and nationwide in Denmark 2008-21 (n=3,415,915; 6 years). RESULTS: The incidence was statistically higher for ASCVD than for acute pancreatitis at any plasma triglycerides up to 30 mmol/L (2,657 mg/dL) in all cohorts, while nationwide in Denmark the incidence of acute pancreatitis was nominally higher than that of ASCVD at triglycerides of 50 mmol/L (4,429 mg/dL) or higher. In women, age-adjusted incidence rates per 1,000 person-years per 1 mmol/L (89 mg/dL) higher plasma triglycerides across all levels were 1.8(95% confidence interval 1.2-2.3) for ASCVD versus 0.1(0.02-0.2) for acute pancreatitis in the CCHS 1976-78, 1.9(1.2-2.5) versus 0.1(0.01-0.2) in the CCHS 1991-94, 0.9(0.7-1.0) versus 0.1(0.1-0.1) in the CGPS, 0.6(0.6-0.7) versus 0.2(0.2-0.2) in the UK Biobank, and 0.4(0.4-0.5) versus 0.05(0.04-0.05) nationwide in Denmark. Corresponding values in men were 1.5(1.0-2.0) versus 0.1(0.1-0.1), 0.9(0.5-1.3) versus 0.04(0-0.1), 1.1(0.9-1.3) versus 0.04(0-0.08), 1.1(1.0-1.2) versus 0.1(0.1-0.1), and 0.6(0.5-0.6) versus 0.05(0.05-0.06), respectively. CONCLUSIONS: The incidence of ASCVD was statistically higher than that of acute pancreatitis up to triglycerides of 30 mmol/L (2,657 mg/dL), while acute pancreatitis was nominally higher than ASCVD at 50 mmol/L (4,429 mg/dL) or higher.

10.1016/j.atherosclerosis.2026.121947.title: Elevated remnant cholesterol and risk of heart failure in the general population
10.1016/j.atherosclerosis.2026.121947.abstract: AIMS: Elevated remnant cholesterol is a causal risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Here, we tested the hypothesis that high levels of remnant cholesterol are observationally associated with increased risk of heart failure in individuals in the general population with and without statin therapy. METHODS AND RESULTS: We included 108,500 and 428,922 individuals free of baseline heart failure from the Copenhagen General Population Study (CGPS) and the UK Biobank, two cohort studies of the adult Danish and UK general populations started in 2003-2015 and 2006-2010. During median 9.2 and 13.7 years of follow-up, 5321(4.9%) and 21,428(4.3%) developed heart failure in the two studies. Diagnoses of heart failure were retrieved from Danish and UK national health registers. For individuals with and without statin therapy and in both the CGPS and the UK Biobank, stepwise higher remnant cholesterol were associated with stepwise increasing risk of a diagnosis of heart failure. For individuals without statin therapy, those with remnant cholesterol ≥1.5 mmol/L(≥59 mg/dL) compared to those with remnant cholesterol <0.5 mmol/L(<19 mg/dL), the multivariable adjusted hazard ratios for risk of heart failure were 1.40(95% confidence interval: 1.19-1.63) in the CGPS and 1.61(1.38-1.89) in the UK Biobank. Corresponding hazard ratios for individuals with statin therapy were 1.63(1.29-2.07) and 1.60(1.24-2.07), respectively. CONCLUSION: In 108,500 and 428,922 individuals from the general populations of Denmark and the UK, stepwise higher levels of remnant cholesterol were associated with stepwise increasing risk of heart failure in individuals with and without statin therapy.

10.4244/eij-d-26-00473.title: Guided P2Y12 inhibitor selection after rapid CYP2C19 genotyping in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention
10.4244/eij-d-26-00473.abstract: Background: Dual antiplatelet therapy remains the standard treatment following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). While prasugrel and ticagrelor offer consistent antiplatelet effects, they increase bleeding risk compared with clopidogrel, which requires CYP2C19 bioactivation. Aims: This study aimed to evaluate the impact of rapid CYP2C19 genotyping at the time of PCI on P2Y 12 inhibitor selection and clinical outcomes in real-world patients. Methods: A total of 974 patients who underwent PCI and rapid CYP2C19 genotyping and received P2Y 12 inhibitor treatment were included. P2Y 12 inhibitor selection, P2Y 12 inhibitor switching, major atherothrombotic events (MAE; a composite of all-cause death, myocardial infarction, ischaemic stroke, stent thrombosis, or unstable angina requiring revascularisation), and bleeding events were assessed throughout the first year post-PCI. Time-varying Cox regression analysis was performed to assess event risk in patients treated with clopidogrel (reference) versus prasugrel/ticagrelor after stratifying by loss-of-function (LOF) status and adjusting for stratum-specific confounders. Results: Clopidogrel was prescribed more frequently at discharge among CYP2C19 non-LOF versus LOF carriers (43% [296/691] vs 31% [87/283]; p<0.001). The median duration of follow-up was 359 days (interquartile range [IQR] 190-362 days). Among LOF allele carriers de-escalating to clopidogrel, the median de-escalation time was 180 days (IQR 92-354 days). MAE were not significantly different between P2Y 12 inhibitor regimens after stratifying by LOF status (LOF-prasugrel/ticagrelor [n=147] vs LOF-clopidogrel [n=136]: adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 0.87 [95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.36-2.10]; non-LOF-prasugrel/ticagrelor [n=272] vs non-LOF-clopidogrel [n=419]: adjusted HR 1.26, 95% CI: 0.67-2.36). No significant differences in Bleeding Academic Research Consortium bleeding events were observed. Conclusions: This real-world study shows that, among LOF carriers managed with rapid CYP2C19 genotyping and delayed de-escalation, ischaemic and bleeding event rates were not significantly different between those taking clopidogrel versus those taking prasugrel/ticagrelor, though findings should be interpreted cautiously.

10.4244/eij-d-26-00575.title: Prediction of coronary events by computed tomography-derived Murray law-based quantitative flow ratio
10.4244/eij-d-26-00575.abstract: Background: Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA)-derived Murray law-based quantitative flow ratio (CT-μFR) provides a non-invasive measure of vessel-level ischaemia but may not capture local haemodynamic abnormalities reflected by the longitudinal pressure gradient across the lesion (CT-μFR gradient). Aims: We aimed to evaluate the association of CT-μFR and the CT-μFR gradient with 3-year vessel-level subsequent coronary events and to determine the incremental prognostic value of their combined assessment. Methods: Our study included a total of 885 vessels from 312 patients who underwent invasive coronary angiography for acute coronary syndrome (ACS) or stable angina and had prior CCTA performed 6 months to 3 years earlier. CT-μFR and the CT-μFR gradient were assessed by an independent core laboratory blinded to the clinical data. The primary outcome was 3-year subsequent coronary events (a composite of vessel-specific myocardial infarction or urgent revascularisation for ACS). The discrimination ability of predictive models was assessed using Harrell’s C-index. Results: Vessels with CT-μFR ≤0.80 or a CT-μFR gradient ≥0.004/mm had a higher risk of events than those with CT-μFR>0.80 (79.1% vs 20.4%, adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 6.87, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 5.26-8.96; p<0.001) or a CT-μFR gradient <0.004/mm (72.6% vs 27.4%, adjusted HR 4.08, 95% CI: 3.15-5.28; p<0.001), respectively. Among vessels with CT-μFR>0.80, a CT-μFR gradient ≥0.004/mm remained associated with increased risk (adjusted HR 2.59, 95% CI: 1.63-4.11; p<0.001). Adding the CT-μFR gradient to CT-μFR improved discrimination in the overall cohort (C-index 0.700 to 0.755; p<0.001) as well as the subgroup with CT-μFR>0.80 (C-index 0.575 to 0.655; p<0.001). Conclusions: Both CT-μFR and the CT-μFR gradient are independently associated with 3-year subsequent coronary events. Their combined assessment improves risk stratification beyond CT-μFR alone. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT04794868)

10.4244/eij-d-26-00457.title: Prognostic value of Murray law-based quantitative flow ratio after percutaneous coronary intervention
10.4244/eij-d-26-00457.abstract: Background: Post-percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) physiological indices have prognostic relevance. Murray law-based quantitative flow ratio (μQFR) enables wire-free, rapid, single-view functional assessment, yet its long-term prognostic value after PCI remains incompletely established. Aims: We sought to evaluate the prognostic value of post-PCI μQFR for long-term adverse outcomes. Methods: This prespecified subgroup analysis of the FAVOR III China trial included 3,825 patients. All PCI-treated vessels with a reference diameter ≥2.5 mm and 50-90% diameter stenosis were analysed for offline post-PCI μQFR. The primary endpoint was 5-year major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; including death from any cause, myocardial infarction, or ischaemia-driven revascularisation). Results: Post-PCI μQFR was successfully analysed in 4,196 vessels from 3,455 patients, with similar distributions between the randomised treatment groups. At 5 years, a low post-PCI μQFR was associated with a higher incidence of MACE compared with the intermediate and high post-PCI μQFR tertiles (23.1% vs 19.0% vs 17.2%; p=0.001). Using the highest tertile (μQFR>0.95) as a reference, adjusted hazard ratios (aHR) were 1.08 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.87-1.34) for the intermediate tertile (0.92-0.95) and 1.30 (95% CI: 1.06-1.60) for the lowest tertile (μQFR ≤0.91). Using a receiver operating characteristic-derived cutoff, MACE occurred more frequently in patients with post-PCI μQFR <0.94 (22.3% vs 17.4%, aHR 1.23, 95% CI: 1.04-1.47; p=0.02) than in those with post-PCI μQFR ≥0.94. No significant interaction was observed between treatment strategy and post-PCI μQFR (p for interaction=0.23). Conclusions: Post-PCI μQFR distributions were similar between treatment groups, but lower values were associated with higher 5-year adverse event risk without significant treatment interaction. Its limited binary discrimination supports use as a continuous metric for post-PCI physiological risk stratification. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT03656848)
